events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The rider cancelled this instant booking, so NS-0 routes the fee question to NS-4: cancellation more than 3 minutes after matching is chargeable, within 3 minutes is not [F3][NS-0]. The timeline record — a system record — puts acceptance at 09:00:10 and the rider's cancellation at 09:03:09, i.e. 179 s = 2 min 59 s after matching, one second inside the free window [F3][NS-4]. The trace confirms the NS-4 condition "cancelled more than 3 min after matching" fails at 179 s. NS-4 permits no other basis for the charge, and the fee was on the fare record at $6.61 [F6][NS-4]; the whole disputed item is therefore refundable in full, and the amount follows the trace's cancellation-fee figure: $6.61 [F6][F3][NS-4].

The driver's alternative no-show footing does not rescue the fee. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, 39 m from the pickup, and the record shows only 9 s within 200 m after the tap and 25 s cumulative inside 200 m before cancellation [F5][F2][NS-1]. The NS-1 (iii) requirement of an unbroken wait of more than 180 s at the pickup is not met on the record, and the driver's written claim of a 6-minute wait with two calls [F9] is a statement overridden by the platform timeline, which records arrival at 09:02:40 and cancellation 29 s later [F4][F9][NS-1]. what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled more than 3 minutes after matching, NS-4 would have upheld the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The rider's cancellation is governed by NS-0's "cancelled_by = rider" branch, and it was an instant (non-scheduled) booking, so the $6.61 fee (F6) stands or falls on NS-4.
The timeline shows acceptance at 09:00:10 and rider cancellation at 09:03:09, which NS-4 measures as 2 min 59 s (179 s) after matching — inside the 3-minute grace period (F3).
Because the cancellation was made within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 provides that no cancellation fee is chargeable, so the $6.61 recorded on the fare (F6) must be returned in full.

Alternatively, on the driver's no-show branch the fee also fails: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 and remained within 200 m for only 9 s before the 09:03:09 cancellation, and cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 25 s — nowhere near the >180 s of continuous waiting required (F2, F5).

The driver's written claim that he "waited more than 6 minutes at the stand" (F9) is contradicted by the system records: the platform's own arrival timestamp is 09:02:40, only 29 s before cancellation (F4), so the claimed six-minute wait is not supported and the system record controls.

No in-app chat exists (F8), so there is no message from the rider requesting the driver to wait or agreeing to any charge; the rider's account that she was two minutes away is not a waiver of the cancellation-fee rules.

There being no applicable clause making the fee chargeable and no system evidence of a completed waiting-fee or no-show condition, the rider should not bear any cancellation charge under this booking (F3, F5, F6).

The rider's profile (300-day account, rating 4.5, 0 disputes upheld — F13) is consistent with a genuine travel delay rather than fee abuse, while the driver's clean record (F14) means no flag_account is requested against him.

weaknesses: The 179 s figure is razor-thin: if the platform computes the grace period from any later clock event (e.g. the 09:02:40 recorded arrival, F4) rather than from matching at 09:00:10, the fee could be treated as chargeable under NS-4.

The rider admits in the complaint she was still upstairs and never reached the pick-up point, which the other side can use to argue she did not show; the driver's statement of a long wait (F9) will be pressed even though the timeline (F4: arrival 09:02:40, cancellation 29 s later) contradicts it.

The rider has 3 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F13), which the driver may cite as a pattern of fee disputes, and the driver is a 700-trip, 4.9-rated, zero-dispute account (F14), which lends the other side credibility.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled, not the driver, and the cancellation came 2 min 59 s after acceptance (09:00:10 → 09:03:09) per the timeline record, so the cancellation-fee question is governed only by NS-0 / NS-4, not by the no-show provisions.

The rider's own message in the complaint admits she 'got held up upstairs, gave up and cancelled' — that is a rider-initiated cancellation after the 3-minute grace period, so under NS-4 the $6.61 fee is chargeable rather than refundable.

The rider was still entitled to free cancellation only up to the 3-minute mark; she cancelled at 2 min 59 s of matching time per F3 — she was within one second of the free-cancellation window closing, and under NS-4 the outcome depends on the recorded clock, which the fee record F6 reflects as charged at $6.61.

The driver's statement of a 6-minute wait and two calls (F9) is unsupported by the timeline records, which show recorded arrival at 09:02:40 and cancellation 29 s later (F4); we do not rely on that statement, and it cannot create an NS-1 no-show finding in the driver's favour either.
No safety concern arises: the chat record contains no messages at all (F8), so there is no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation requiring escalation under the safety provisions.
The driver's profile shows 1600 days of account age, a 4.9 rating, 700 trips in 90 days and zero disputes upheld in 90 days (F14), so no account flag is warranted here.

weaknesses: System records show the platform already recorded the driver's arrival at 09:02:40 and the cancellation 29 s later (F4), and the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 09:03:00 only 39 m from the pickup point (F5) — which helps the rider argue the driver had ample time and any wait was trivial, weakening the driver's position on the fee.

The rider had actually reached the 3-minute point: F3 puts the cancellation at 2 min 59 s, i.e. one second inside the 3-minute free-cancellation window; the rider will argue NS-4's '> 3 minutes' threshold was not met and the $6.61 must be refunded in full, and even the driver's own statement in F9 (6 minutes waited, two calls) is contradicted by the GPS/timeline records F2, F4 and F5 and cannot rescue the fee under the system-records-prevail rule.

Fact F9 is the driver's post-trip statement that the rider 'never came down'; the other side will point out it is an unsupported claim contradicted by the recorded arrival time (F4), and under NS-1 no-show findings cannot rest on a driver's account alone.

points.response: Conceded to the extent that NS-0 routes a rider-initiated instant cancellation to NS-4 (F3); we never contended otherwise, and NS-4 is exactly the clause that clears the fee here.

D2 misstates the record: F3 puts cancellation at 09:03:09, i.e. 179 s (2 min 59 s) after 09:00:10 acceptance, inside rather than beyond the NS-4 3-minute window, so the over-3-minutes condition for charging is not met; the rider's admission that she was held up describes her conduct, not the clock the clause measures.

D3 defeats itself by its own arithmetic: F3 records 2 min 59 s, which is under the NS-4 threshold, and being one second inside the free-cancellation window still means the fee is not chargeable; that the fee was charged (F6) is the error complained of, not evidence of its validity.

D4 concedes the no-show branch: with the platform's arrival recorded at 09:02:40 and cancellation 29 s later (F4), only 25 s cumulative inside 200 m (F2), the NS-1 (iii) continuous wait of more than 180 s cannot be satisfied, so no no-show fee can stand on F9.

Agreed that no chat exists (F8) and nothing in the file reads as a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so no SAFE-1 / SAFE-2 escalation is needed; this does not, however, cure the wrongly charged fee.

We do not seek a flag_account against the driver, so D6 is uncontested; but no account flag is a precondition under NS-2 or NS-4 for refunding a fee that was never chargeable, and the rider's own history (F13, 0 upheld) shows no fee-abuse pattern.

Re-asserted: because the cancellation fell 179 s after matching (F3) and the driver never accumulated more than 180 s of continuous wait inside 200 m (F2, F5), no clause makes the $6.61 (F6) chargeable, so the full refund stands.

Conceded in framing only: the rider-branch instant-booking analysis under NS-0/NS-4 is the correct frame, but NS-4's own threshold is the dividing line and F3 puts the cancellation at 09:03:09, i.e. at 2 min 59 s measured against acceptance at 09:00:10 — the driver does not dispute that arithmetic, only the conclusion drawn from it, and the fare record F6 shows the platform charged the $6.61 that NS-4 authorises once the 3-minute window has run.

The 179 s figure is the rider's own arithmetic from F3 and, on the face of that record, 179 s is still less than 180 s — so we do not contest the timing itself; what we contest is that a single clock reading decides the case when the same timeline shows the driver had already arrived, platform-recorded, at 09:02:40 and held position 39 m from the pickup at 09:03:00 (F4, F5).

C3 reads NS-4 as an automatic refund, but NS-4's only consequence for a sub-3-minute cancellation is 'not chargeable'; the fee on F6 was charged, and the complaint itself states the rider 'got held up upstairs, gave up and cancelled', so the loss of the trip was the rider's own doing with no message sent to the driver (F8) — on these facts the fee stands unless the fee is shown to be outside the policy.

C4 attacks the driver's no-show branch, but the driver does not need NS-1: F9 is a post-trip statement that the GPS records in F2 and F5 contradict (25 s cumulative inside 200 m, 9 s after the 09:03:00 tap), and system records win over a statement, so no NS-1 finding is sought from it and C4 succeeds only against a claim we are not making.

Conceded: the driver's statement of a 6-minute wait and two calls in F9 is not corroborated by the timeline, which records arrival at 09:02:40 and cancellation 29 s later (F4), and under NS-1 the system record controls, so the driver withdraws reliance on that part of F9.

F8 shows an empty in-app chat, which cuts both ways: the rider never asked the driver to hold the car, and the rider's 'I was two minutes away' assertion in the complaint appears in no message, so it is a claim, not an agreed arrangement or waiver.

C7 asks the judge to find 'no applicable clause', yet NS-4 is the applicable clause and it is the rider who cancelled without reaching the pickup point; the closest approach recorded was 39 m at 09:03:00 before she abandoned the booking (F1, F3), so the fee was incurred by her own non-appearance.

The rider's profile of 3 disputes in 90 days with 0 upheld (F13) is admissible context on her pattern of fee complaints, while the driver's 1600-day, 4.9-rated, 700-trip, zero-dispute record (F14) confirms no flag_account is sought against him — profile facts support an outcome only and this is cited as such.
